| | Hi Peter – before I ask you to chip in to help me win in Ohio and keep the Senate blue, I need to take a moment to explain why I'm in this fight and what your grassroots contribution would mean today.

I grew up in Mansfield, Ohio, in a community of ironworkers, carpenters, autoworkers, and electricians. I spent summers working on my family's farm. Today, I live in Cleveland with my wife, Connie, and our two rescue dogs, Franklin and Walter.

**I’ll be honest with you, Peter:** Over the years, in Ohio, we've seen manufacturing jobs shipped overseas because of bad trade deals, prices skyrocketing as wages failed to keep up, and hopes for a comfortable retirement dashed. That's why I've devoted my life to fighting for the Dignity of Work – the idea that hard work should pay off for everyone, no matter who you are, where you live, or what kind of work you do.

**Every day in the Senate, I’m fighting for _you._ But I’m facing my toughest race yet, and I need your help to win.** [**_Will you chip in $25 or more now – split between my campaign and the Democratic Party of Georgia – so I can keep up the fight in Ohio and defend the Senate for Democrats?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65628589/414067095/-843865763?refcode=20230629.2_ShB_6AU&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZTAwY2RmZC1hMjE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Fmbw-dLaSaN_h2Y17dQKisLKYUvMpAJyxfWPfrrPFSY=)**_

Right now, Mitch McConnell and the GOP need to flip only two seats to retake Senate control – and experts at _Politico_ say it could all come down to Ohio. Last year’s Senate race here was one of the most costly in the nation, and _NBC News_ reports this one could be “even nastier and more expensive.”

**That's why I simply cannot win this race – and Democrats simply cannot hold on to our narrow Senate majority – without grassroots support from folks like you. As one of the most vulnerable senators in the country, I'm personally asking:**

[**_Will you please split $25 between my campaign and the Democratic Party of Georgia to help us hit our End of Quarter fundraising goal, power our reelection campaign to victory, and keep the Senate blue?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65628590/414067096/-843865763?refcode=20230629.2_ShB_6AU&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjZTAwY2RmZC1hMjE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Fmbw-dLaSaN_h2Y17dQKisLKYUvMpAJyxfWPfrrPFSY=)**_

This is gonna be a heck of a fight, but with you by my side, I know we can beat the odds and continue making much-needed progress for workers and families. Thanks for being on our team.

With gratitude,

Sherrod

This fall, we hope to elect leaders that will proudly represent the true needs of our Commonwealth’s historically disenfranchised and neglected communities. The only way to make that happen is by engaging Black, Indigenous, and other people of color, immigrants, and the youth in order to make their voices heard. Friend,

I’ve spoken with young people across the country about the issues that affect them today: Debilitating medical and student loan debt. Attacks on basic human rights for women and members of the LGBTQ+ community. Widespread gun violence. A rapidly warming planet. The future they face is uncertain and volatile.

It doesn’t have to be this way. Politicians have the power and the obligation to make the world better for future generations. That’s why I’ve spent my career advocating for the policies that will move this country forward and provide for the youth of America.

Will you stand with me in fighting for a country our young people deserve? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/american-youth-video]

We need to cancel student debt and give young people the financial freedom to own a home and pursue the American Dream. We need common-sense gun reform and a Green New Deal. We need legislation that will explicitly protect the right to choose, the right to medical care, and the right to thrive regardless of who you are or who you love.

Friend, I’ve been committed to supporting families for a long time, including back when I was a state legislator. For example, after I breastfed my son while on the Michigan House floor, I introduced legislation to ban discrimination against women who breastfeed in public. In Congress, I’ve founded and now co-chair the Mamas’ Caucus, and I’m a founding member of the Dads’ Caucus too. We recently hosted events around Father’s Day to talk about the policies we need to uplift working-class families, such as providing affordable childcare and paid leave, reducing poverty and ensuring pay equity, and addressing the unjust maternal and infant health disparities faced by Black women and other mothers of color. [**I’m committed to making the bold changes that working-class families and families of color deserve. Friend,
It is shameful that in the richest nation in the history of the world, children are going to bed hungry. The costs of raising a child in our country are among the highest in the world, and the U.S. is also one of the only industrialized countries that does not offer a single day of paid family or medical leave.
With systemic racism in our country’s reproductive care, we’re also facing a Black maternal and infant health crisis. Black infants are more than twice as likely to die as white infants—a disparity greater than existed in 1850. Black women are also three times more likely to die during pregnancy than white women.
**As a mama and founder of the Mamas’ Caucus in Congress, I refuse to accept this status quo.**

I’m committed to making the transformative changes that families of color and working-class families deserve.
For example, more than 30 million workers do not have access to a single day of paid leave. That includes 67% of low-wage workers, most of whom are women and people of color.
Clearly, our country’s policies and institutions have too often failed families of color, and this needs to change.
**In partnership with Mothering Justice, I founded the Mamas’ Caucus to include women of color in the legislative decisions that impact them and their loved ones. We’re committed to advocating for all mothers that have been excluded from policymaking for so long.**
With the Mamas’ Caucus and the newly established Dads’ Caucus, we’re building partnerships in Congress to fight for policies that support every family, including a national paid leave program and providing high-quality childcare and early education programs that pay providers a living wage.
We’re also advocating for legislation to lift people out of poverty, such as my bill the _End Child Poverty Act_ , which would provide families with close to a $400/month payment per child, cutting deep child poverty by 70%.
Policies like this will make it easier for working class people to afford necessities like diapers and childcare, and will provide a long overdue social safety net for our nation’s working families and children.

clean_body: uplifting working-class families | | | Friend, I’ve been committed to supporting families for a long time, including back when I was a state legislator. For example, after I breastfed my son while on the Michigan House floor, I introduced legislation to ban discrimination against women who breastfeed in public. In Congress, I’ve founded and now co-chair the Mamas’ Caucus, and I’m a founding member of the Dads’ Caucus too. We recently hosted events around Father’s Day to talk about the policies we need to uplift working-class families, such as providing affordable childcare and paid leave, reducing poverty and ensuring pay equity, and addressing the unjust maternal and infant health disparities faced by Black women and other mothers of color. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately: | | | | | | | | | | Thank you. Please feel free to check out yesterday’s email for more information. In solidarity, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib** Date: Wed, Jun 28, 2023 Subject: the U.S. is one of the only industrialized countries that does not offer a single day of paid family or medical leave. To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, It is shameful that in the richest nation in the history of the world, children are going to bed hungry. The costs of raising a child in our country are among the highest in the world, and the U.S. is also one of the only industrialized countries that does not offer a single day of paid family or medical leave. With systemic racism in our country’s reproductive care, we’re also facing a Black maternal and infant health crisis. Black infants are more than twice as likely to die as white infants—a disparity greater than existed in 1850. Black women are also three times more likely to die during pregnancy than white women. As a mama and founder of the Mamas’ Caucus in Congress, I refuse to accept this status quo. I’m making sure that we center mothers of color in the policies we champion in Congress, from reducing poverty and reinstating the child tax credit, to closing the racial and gender wealth gap, to ensuring a national paid family and medical leave program, to investing in affordable childcare, to establishing healthcare equity and housing for all. I’m committed to making the transformative changes that families of color and working-class families deserve. For example, more than 30 million workers do not have access to a single day of paid leave. That includes 67% of low-wage workers, most of whom are women and people of color. Clearly, our country’s policies and institutions have too often failed families of color, and this needs to change. In partnership with Mothering Justice, I founded the Mamas’ Caucus to include women of color in the legislative decisions that impact them and their loved ones. We’re committed to advocating for all mothers that have been excluded from policymaking for so long. With the Mamas’ Caucus and the newly established Dads’ Caucus, we’re building partnerships in Congress to fight for policies that support every family, including a national paid leave program and providing high-quality childcare and early education programs that pay providers a living wage. We’re also advocating for legislation to lift people out of poverty, such as my bill the End Child Poverty Act , which would provide families with close to a $400/month payment per child, cutting deep child poverty by 70%. Policies like this will make it easier for working class people to afford necessities like diapers and childcare, and will provide a long overdue social safety net for our nation’s working families and children. Under SB 1718 in Florida:
* Entering into Florida with someone who’s undocumented will become a crime
* Emergency rooms and hospitals will be required to ask for data on patients’ immigration statuses
* Local governments are no longer allowed to provide funds for community IDs
* Expanded use of the flawed E-Verify system will infringe on people’s right to work

As extreme Republican-led states continue to attack and scapegoat immigrant communities with cruel laws like this, **we need to protect each other.**
In Florida and beyond, we’re reaching immigrant communities to make sure they have all the info they need to thrive. From our revamped “Know Your Rights” campaign to the webinars we’re hosting, our resources are intended to make sure everyone can continue living their lives freely.
But SB 1718 won’t be the last cruel law we see impact immigrants, so we need to be ready to mobilize and deliver resources no matter what anti-immigrant leaders come up with next. That’s why I’m reaching out to you today:

Derek, you may not know this, but before I was a representative in the House, I was an engineer.

Some might say that jumping from a career in science and technology to one in politics might seem odd. But my years using my STEM education and in public service have taught me that the two realms have a lot in common. Looking to the data, rejecting misinformation, questioning one’s own biases – these are part of a STEM professional’s toolkit and should be part of a politician’s, too.
****But right now, for too many of my colleagues in Congress, science and truth seem to take a back seat to ideology. I’m committed to defending the principles of inquiry and truth in the House, but I can only continue to do so with your support – which is why I’m reaching out ahead of my end-of-quarter deadline.[ Please, Derek, will you make a gift of $5 to ensure I can fight for evidence-based change?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65630390/414072377/685235109?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk842-fr-nd&recurring=0&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYzU0MDVjMC1hNjE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7c7c2EkD5PnGlYFZmsNFANDb64A6IS-ufljpuIvA-t4=)**[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65630393/414072380/685235109?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk842-fr-nd&recurring=0&amount=5&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NDkxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlYzU0MDVjMC1hNjE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=7c7c2EkD5PnGlYFZmsNFANDb64A6IS-ufljpuIvA-t4=)**
I can already see that I’ve used my background to pass legislation that helps Americans. Last year, I helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act, which makes historic investments in clean energy and is expected to reduce emissions by approximately 40% by 2030 – and I helped pass the CHIPS Act, which made our supply chains more resilient and helped us to outcompete China.
I’ve also spearheaded the Women in STEM and Bipartisan Climate Solutions caucuses to foster exchange and productive policymaking. In this age of misinformation, it seems like everything is being put up to dispute for political reasons – from climate science to COVID-19, election legitimacy to economic policy. **I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished so far, but to face these troubling trends, we need more solution-oriented, logic and data-based approaches to passing legislation that will help American families.**
**I’d like to think I’ve been doing this so far.** But I can only continue to do so with the support of this grassroots team. **The 2024 elections are closer than they seem, and now’s the best time for us to gather our resources to ensure we can continue to spread our message of truth, justice, and progress.[Please, Derek, can I count on your support ahead of my end-of-quarter deadline? clean_body: | | | Derek, you may not know this, but before I was a representative in the House, I was an engineer. Some might say that jumping from a career in science and technology to one in politics might seem odd. But my years using my STEM education and in public service have taught me that the two realms have a lot in common. Looking to the data, rejecting misinformation, questioning one’s own biases – these are part of a STEM professional’s toolkit and should be part of a politician’s, too. **But right now, for too many of my colleagues in Congress, science and truth seem to take a back seat to ideology. I’m committed to defending the principles of inquiry and truth in the House, but I can only continue to do so with your support – which is why I’m reaching out ahead of my end-of-quarter deadline.= I can already see that I’ve used my background to pass legislation that helps Americans. Last year, I helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act, which makes historic investments in clean energy and is expected to reduce emissions by approximately 40% by 2030 – and I helped pass the CHIPS Act, which made our supply chains more resilient and helped us to outcompete China. I’ve also spearheaded the Women in STEM and Bipartisan Climate Solutions caucuses to foster exchange and productive policymaking. In this age of misinformation, it seems like everything is being put up to dispute for political reasons – from climate science to COVID-19, election legitimacy to economic policy. I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished so far, but to face these troubling trends, we need more solution-oriented, logic and data-based approaches to passing legislation that will help American families. I’d like to think I’ve been doing this so far. But I can only continue to do so with the support of this grassroots team. The 2024 elections are closer than they seem, and now’s the best time for us to gather our resources to ensure we can continue to spread our message of truth, justice, and progress.=** | | = Thank you. John Joseph Pershing was born in September 1860 near Laclede, Missouri. After completing high school in 1878, he became a teacher of local African American students. He also studied at the State Normal School, now Truman State University, graduating in 1880, then competed for appointment to the United States Military Academy. Pershing spent his first years in the military fighting in U.S. campaigns against the Apache and Sioux Native Americans in New Mexico and Arizona, although he and his unit did not participate in the Wounded Knee Massacre.

subject: The hardest part about running for Congress
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Allyson for Congress
body:
Friends,

Every day, when I talk to voters on a call, at a local event or even on the street in my neighborhood, I’m reminded of why I’m campaigning for Congress and of my life’s mission:

PUBLIC SERVICE.

You may hear a ton of politicians proclaiming to be public servants, but I think most of them don’t get what that actually means. That’s one of the reasons why there’s so many issues in our country and this district, CA-40 .

I’m running because I believe a member of Congress’ first and only priority should be SERVING PEOPLE; not corporate interests, or partisan hawks.

The hardest part about running for Congress, I’ll be honest, is fundraising .

I’ve learned that there are certain deadlines, like the FEC end-of-quarter one coming up this Friday on June 30, that are super important to meet in terms of fundraising metrics. That’s why I’m asking you for your donation again.

DONATE >> https://secure.actblue.com/donate/loc_email_2023q2?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2023.06.29_B1_EOQ1

And this one is particularly important because media groups and other political players pay very close attention to the amount fundraised at the end-of-quarters.

It shows the grassroots strength of a campaign. So far I’m incredibly proud of the support I’ve received from my community and friends. Many have donated and from the bottom of my heart I’m truly grateful for your support.

With congressional campaigns, MOMENTUM is incredibly important. So let’s keep it going! Even if you’ve pitched in already, I need your continued support.

Friends, if you can pitch in before the FEC end-of-quarter June 30 deadline this Friday, I’d really appreciate it.

DONATE >> https://secure.actblue.com/donate/loc_email_2023q2?refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2023.06.29_B1_EOQ1

Thank you, thank you and thank YOU!

– Allyson

**But, Peter, it has been a little jarring going from the majority to the minority – the GOP-led House has shown itself to be dysfunctional at best, harmful at worst. In fact, recently Jim Jordan’s Judiciary Committee spent hours passing feel-good resolutions for National Police Week while failing to vote for _any_ legislation that would fund federal law enforcement agencies like the Department of Justice and the FBI.**

| A native Floridian with blue-collar roots, Ron was raised in Dunedin by his mother, a nurse, and father, who installed cable boxes. He attended Dunedin High School and worked his way through Yale University, where he was the captain of the varsity baseball team. He also graduated with honors from Harvard Law School, where he earned a commission in the U.S. Navy as a JAG officer.

During his active-duty service, Ron deployed to Iraq in support of the SEAL mission in Fallujah, Ramadi and the rest of Al Anbar province. His military decorations include the Bronze Star Medal for Meritorious Service and the Iraq Campaign Medal.
---
Ron also served as a prosecutor in Florida, where he put child predators behind bars. He was elected to Congress in 2012 on a platform of government accountability, advocating for term limits and a balanced budget amendment.

In Congress, DeSantis spearheaded the fight to expose the weaponization of the IRS against conservatives. He also fought to hold accountable the rogue federal agencies involved in manufacturing the "Russia collusion" conspiracy theory. As a veteran, DeSantis was a champion for those who have served our country, pushing for reforms to the VA to better serve veterans and expand support for mental health.

In 2018, Ron DeSantis was elected the 46th Governor of Florida. As governor, he has fought for what's right and taken the arrows for the people he represents. During the darkest days of 2020, when the corrupt establishment, bureaucracy, and corporate media united to force lockdowns and mandates on Americans, DeSantis stood up for freedom - even when it wasn't popular.

Grounded in his unshakeable belief in America's founding principles, Governor DeSantis has enacted a bold agenda to transform Florida into a blueprint for the Nation's revival. Governor DeSantis has delivered win after win on conservative priorities:
* Saving livelihoods from job-killing lockdowns and vaccine mandates,

* Protecting citizens from the harmful impacts of Biden's border crisis by enacting E-Verify and other bold policies against illegal immigration, such as banning sanctuary cities,

* Defending parental rights and eliminating CRT,

* Defunding DEI bureaucracy in higher ed and holding tenured professors accountable,

* Waging war on woke power-grabs like ESG and central bank digital currency,

* Enacting the strongest medical freedom laws in the nation,

* Turning Florida into a model for election integrity,

* Protecting the unborn,

* Standing up for the 2nd Amendment by making Florida a constitutional carry state,

* Expanding education freedom,

* Prohibiting land purchases by the CCP and related individuals and entities,

* Lowering prescription drug costs,

* Holding woke corporations and school unions accountable,

* Creating a universal school choice program,

* Delivering record-breaking tax relief,

* Helping families achieve the American dream of homeownership,

* Supporting law enforcement and our veterans,

* Enacting tougher penalties for drug dealers and sex offenders,

* Appointing seven conservative justices to the Florida Supreme Court,

* ...and so much more.

After leading Florida with common sense and conviction throughout his first term, DeSantis delivered a record-setting victory of nearly 20 points in 2022. He earned his second term by the largest raw vote margin in state history, winning by more than 1.5 million votes.

But history didn't stop there:

Governor DeSantis flipped Miami-Dade County red, winning the majority-Hispanic urban county by double digits. Conventional wisdom assumed this was impossible for a Republican - as recently as 2016, Hillary Clinton won Miami-Dade County by nearly 30 points.

Governor DeSantis flipped several other blue counties red, including Palm Beach County. He won 62 out of 67 counties overall.

Compared to his first statewide election in 2018, Governor DeSantis was up +19% with Independents, up +30% with Hispanics, and up +9% with women.

Governor DeSantis delivered a record-setting victory with battle-tested leadership, a bold policy agenda, and never backing down to corporate media or special interests. As he said at his inauguration: "When the world lost its mind - when common sense suddenly became an uncommon virtue - Florida was a refuge of sanity, a citadel of freedom for our fellow Americans and even for people around the world. In captaining the ship of state, we choose to navigate the boisterous sea of liberty rather than cower in the calm docks of despotism."

Governor DeSantis has ensured that Florida is a free and safe place to raise a family. Thanks to the governor's leadership, Floridians enjoy a low tax burden, quality education opportunities, and a bulwark in place against the Biden Administration's overreach and various elite power grabs that seek to force people to adopt a particular ideology. Thanks to the governor's vision, this year's legislative session delivered the most ambitious conservative policy victories in Florida's history.

This year, Governor DeSantis signed:
* Record tax relief

* ESG prohibitions

* Measures counteracting the influence of the CCP

* The strongest medical freedom protections in the nation.

* Reforms reducing the costs of medications by delivering transparency

* Bold higher education reforms; defunding DEI

* Improvements to our state's infrastructure

* Tough-on-crime, law and order measures, including the death penalty for child rapists

* The strongest measures protecting Florida from Biden's border crisis

* Reforms for paycheck protection , holding accountable wayward school unions

* Prohibitions on centralized digital currencies in Florida

No leader has accomplished more for his state than Governor DeSantis. He is now sharing his bold vision with the country, leading a movement to deliver the Great American Comeback.

Ron is married to Casey DeSantis, an Emmy Award- winning television anchor. Together, they're the proud parents of their daughters, Madison and Mamie, and their son, Mason.

When we send out emails asking for your support, it is not because we want to put even more strain on your finances under Biden's economy; it's because we're honest with our team about where we're at with our fundraising numbers and what more we need to push our momentum forward. We have reached the point in the campaign of our first FEC-mandated end-of-quarter fundraising deadline, and right now, our digital goal is to raise $626,000 between now and 11:59 PM tomorrow. We know that seems like a lot, but to give perspective, "if each person who read this email on our digital distribution list chipped in $47" , we'd more than triple our fundraising goal. If that happened, we wouldn't need to send another fundraising email this month. | | | | | Tomorrow, a report of our fundraising performance for the first quarter of the campaign will be publicly submitted to the FEC, and the strength of our team will be scrutinized by our opponents across the country. We cannot allow our support to dwindle when there is this much on the line. "Our team knows we're asking for a lot, but can we count on your support before the end-of-quarter deadline on Friday?" | | | | We need your help, Peter. We have a deadline, we have a goal, and we have to hit it. Every donation makes a difference to this campaign, and every donor has a spot on this team. Before the end-of-quarter deadline hits tomorrow, please, donate any amount you can: "". With this first report, we are setting the tone for our Great American Comeback and proving to the country that Americans believe freedom is worth fighting for. | | | | | | | | In Freedom, Team DeSantis | Meet Ron DeSantis | | | | | A native Floridian with blue-collar roots, Ron was raised in Dunedin by his mother, a nurse, and father, who installed cable boxes. He attended Dunedin High School and worked his way through Yale University, where he was the captain of the varsity baseball team. He also graduated with honors from Harvard Law School, where he earned a commission in the U.S. Navy as a JAG officer. During his active-duty service, Ron deployed to Iraq in support of the SEAL mission in Fallujah, Ramadi and the rest of Al Anbar province. His military decorations include the Bronze Star Medal for Meritorious Service and the Iraq Campaign Medal. Ron also served as a prosecutor in Florida, where he put child predators behind bars. He was elected to Congress in 2012 on a platform of government accountability, advocating for term limits and a balanced budget amendment. In Congress, DeSantis spearheaded the fight to expose the weaponization of the IRS against conservatives. He also fought to hold accountable the rogue federal agencies involved in manufacturing the "Russia collusion" conspiracy theory. As a veteran, DeSantis was a champion for those who have served our country, pushing for reforms to the VA to better serve veterans and expand support for mental health. In 2018, Ron DeSantis was elected the 46th Governor of Florida. As governor, he has fought for what's right and taken the arrows for the people he represents. During the darkest days of 2020, when the corrupt establishment, bureaucracy, and corporate media united to force lockdowns and mandates on Americans, DeSantis stood up for freedom - even when it wasn't popular. Grounded in his unshakeable belief in America's founding principles, Governor DeSantis has enacted a bold agenda to transform Florida into a blueprint for the Nation's revival. Governor DeSantis has delivered win after win on conservative priorities: Saving livelihoods from job-killing lockdowns and vaccine mandates, Protecting citizens from the harmful impacts of Biden's border crisis by enacting E-Verify and other bold policies against illegal immigration, such as banning sanctuary cities, Defending parental rights and eliminating CRT, Defunding DEI bureaucracy in higher ed and holding tenured professors accountable, Waging war on woke power-grabs like ESG and central bank digital currency, Enacting the strongest medical freedom laws in the nation, Turning Florida into a model for election integrity, Protecting the unborn, Standing up for the 2nd Amendment by making Florida a constitutional carry state, Expanding education freedom, Prohibiting land purchases by the CCP and related individuals and entities, Lowering prescription drug costs, Holding woke corporations and school unions accountable, Creating a universal school choice program, Delivering record-breaking tax relief, Helping families achieve the American dream of homeownership, Supporting law enforcement and our veterans, Enacting tougher penalties for drug dealers and sex offenders, Appointing seven conservative justices to the Florida Supreme Court, ...and so much more. After leading Florida with common sense and conviction throughout his first term, DeSantis delivered a record-setting victory of nearly 20 points in 2022. He earned his second term by the largest raw vote margin in state history, winning by more than 1.5 million votes. But history didn't stop there: Governor DeSantis flipped Miami-Dade County red, winning the majority-Hispanic urban county by double digits. Conventional wisdom assumed this was impossible for a Republican - as recently as 2016, Hillary Clinton won Miami-Dade County by nearly 30 points. Governor DeSantis flipped several other blue counties red, including Palm Beach County. He won 62 out of 67 counties overall. Compared to his first statewide election in 2018, Governor DeSantis was up +19% with Independents, up +30% with Hispanics, and up +9% with women. Governor DeSantis delivered a record-setting victory with battle-tested leadership, a bold policy agenda, and never backing down to corporate media or special interests. As he said at his inauguration: "When the world lost its mind - when common sense suddenly became an uncommon virtue - Florida was a refuge of sanity, a citadel of freedom for our fellow Americans and even for people around the world. In captaining the ship of state, we choose to navigate the boisterous sea of liberty rather than cower in the calm docks of despotism." Governor DeSantis has ensured that Florida is a free and safe place to raise a family. Thanks to the governor's leadership, Floridians enjoy a low tax burden, quality education opportunities, and a bulwark in place against the Biden Administration's overreach and various elite power grabs that seek to force people to adopt a particular ideology. Thanks to the governor's vision, this year's legislative session delivered the most ambitious conservative policy victories in Florida's history. This year, Governor DeSantis signed: Record tax relief ESG prohibitions Measures counteracting the influence of the CCP The strongest medical freedom protections in the nation. Reforms reducing the costs of medications by delivering transparency Bold higher education reforms; defunding DEI Improvements to our state's infrastructure Tough-on-crime, law and order measures, including the death penalty for child rapists The strongest measures protecting Florida from Biden's border crisis Reforms for paycheck protection , holding accountable wayward school unions Prohibitions on centralized digital currencies in Florida No leader has accomplished more for his state than Governor DeSantis. He is now sharing his bold vision with the country, leading a movement to deliver the Great American Comeback. Ron is married to Casey DeSantis, an Emmy Award- winning television anchor. As much as I like Joe Manchin on a personal level, **as long as he represents West Virginia in DC, Chuck Schumer will continue to rule over the Senate with an iron fist.**

Hi Peter,

My name is Arlene Joyce, and I’m reaching out today on behalf of my incredible daughter, Joanna Weiss.

**I could not be more proud of my girl for stepping up and running to represent OC families in Congress!** From founding an organization dedicated to American values and ethics to her _pro bono_ law work, she’s always had an unrelenting desire to make our community the best place it can be. I’m thrilled she decided to take the next step by running for office.

I’ve spent a lot of time canvassing with Jo during past elections, and through that, we’ve had the pleasure of getting to know many of you. I can promise you that my daughter will never stop listening and learning from this community. She’ll take your stories with her to Washington so that she can serve you with the tenacity you deserve. **She’s been a fighter for her entire life, and she’s just getting started!**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65632811/414079516/-1695430967?refcode=em-6.29.23-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDU2NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZmM2ZWQxNzItYWExNi1lZTExLWE5YmItMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FboIvgbzyJVD5O8-WwNHt6HvPBUuNPc8oA1LDWSZGQ0=) _Jo and I on one of our many canvassing shifts._ Jo keeps us updated on what’s going on with her campaign, and she just told me they’re in the middle of an end-of-quarter fundraising push. **Since it’s the end of the quarter, her team has to submit a financial report to the FEC, which will then be made available to the public.**

clean_body: | | | As a pediatrician and a mom, kids are my priority. Running for Congress helped me understand why our children are always an afterthought in public policy decisions. They can’t vote, they don’t have money, and until now, no one was willing to do the hard work to give them a voice in DC. As a former candidate, I know that well-meaning efforts to support children through advocacy and policy development will only get us so far. Kids need political power, and that means a well-funded PAC whose bottom line is children. It's the only way to create the change our children deserve. That’s why my organization’s first Federal Election Commission (FEC) quarterly fundraising deadline is even more important: Because it’s our first chance to show the public there is power behind this movement. Our kids shouldn’t have to worry that they will be gunned down in their classrooms. They shouldn't have to wonder if their planet will be healthy enough for their children and grandchildren to thrive. They shouldn’t have to watch as our democracy continues to be threatened by selfish politicians who only care about their own power. This is an urgent moment for our nation’s children and together we have the chance to do something about it. In recent days, you’ve heard a lot from me and my team, Derek.
I’ll tell you why. I’m running for Senate because I want to get real things done for all Californians. But I also **truly believe that our democracy is in trouble.**
In the last seven years, things have taken place in this country that I never thought I would see in America— an attempted insurrection, the GOP devolving into a destructive cult of personality around a deeply immoral figure, and some of our most precious freedoms stripped away by a high court system packed with partisan and reactionary justices.
But I want you to know that I remain optimistic about our future. We are a deeply resilient country and we will get through this. There will come a time when we look back on this period of history and wonder how someone like Donald Trump ever became president. How soon we get to that point, however, depends on us. It depends on the kind of effort we make to stop him in 2024 and move this country in the right direction. Having another staunch defender of our democracy in the Senate will help.
Tomorrow night, we will reach our FEC fundraising deadline, after which our fundraising numbers will be made public. And emails like these help us raise money to fight back against the cult of the former president. You see, whether you donate $3, $5, or $10, it all adds up and gets us closer to winning this Senate seat, re-electing Joe Biden, and getting real things done.
And you know what else? **MAGA Republicans will be studying these reports looking for any weakness in our campaign.** They are terrified that I’ll be elected to the Senate, because I have the track record of holding the corrupt accountable, and they know they are next.
**So I’m asking, will you please give what you can to help us end this quarter strong? Here’s a link you can use:[secure.actblue.com/donate/jun2023_abs_em](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=jun2023_abs_em.JzRsbz&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_GEN_EOQ_AC90_20230629_PM1_V1_S1&email=&t=4&akid=2778%2E5257348%2EjkJRxd)**
Derek, as I said, I truly believe that our democracy is on fragile ground.
But I also believe that with the support of this team behind me, we will weather the storm, turn this ship around, and bring real change to America.
— Adam

clean_body: | MAGA Republicans will be studying these reports looking for any weakness in our campaign In recent days, you’ve heard a lot from me and my team, Derek. I’ll tell you why. I’m running for Senate because I want to get real things done for all Californians. But I also truly believe that our democracy is in trouble. In the last seven years, things have taken place in this country that I never thought I would see in America— an attempted insurrection, the GOP devolving into a destructive cult of personality around a deeply immoral figure, and some of our most precious freedoms stripped away by a high court system packed with partisan and reactionary justices. But I want you to know that I remain optimistic about our future. We are a deeply resilient country and we will get through this. There will come a time when we look back on this period of history and wonder how someone like Donald Trump ever became president. How soon we get to that point, however, depends on us. It depends on the kind of effort we make to stop him in 2024 and move this country in the right direction. Having another staunch defender of our democracy in the Senate will help. Tomorrow night, we will reach our FEC fundraising deadline, after which our fundraising numbers will be made public. And emails like these help us raise money to fight back against the cult of the former president. You see, whether you donate $3, $5, or $10, it all adds up and gets us closer to winning this Senate seat, re-electing Joe Biden, and getting real things done. And you know what else? MAGA Republicans will be studying these reports looking for any weakness in our campaign. subject: What happens when a poor kid from Pawtucket runs for Congress?
body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP50/1/105455/images/Gabe%20Amo%20Header_V6.png]

Friend,

Sometimes I think about how improbable it is that a person like me could even be running for Congress. After all, I’m the son of a nurse and a small business owner.

Because of hard work, the support of my family and community, and access to scholarships that allowed me to get a high-quality education, I have been able to serve my state and country at the highest levels of government, for two presidents and a governor.

But I’m not rich, and campaigns are expensive. I’m from a hard-working background. I’ve spent my career in public service, so I can’t self-finance this campaign. Like so many others, I’ve still got student loans to pay.

At the end of the day, I’m just like most Rhode Islanders. I care about my community, and I love my home state.

I’m running for office to send someone to the halls of the U.S. Congress who understands Rhode Island and understands how to get things done for the people here from day one.

So, I need your help. Tomorrow is the LAST day of the fundraising quarter. We’re up against opponents who have lots of their own money, and we can’t do this without you. Can I count on you to help us reach our fundraising goal and show that you don’t have to be wealthy to run for office – and win?

I'm glad the U.S. Supreme Court finally laid to rest one of the worst failed experiments in American history: affirmative action.

Fellow American,

With its decision in _Students for Fair Admissions v Harvard_ , handed down on June 29th, America's Supreme Court has finally laid affirmative action to rest. University administrators will surely be weeping at the grave. But what these administrators fail to appreciate is that they themselves may be accomplices in the doctrine's demise. Their weapon of choice was an unusual one: trampling free speech on campus by enacting speech codes, showing bias against students with disfavoured views and disinviting controversial speakers. Unusual, but deadly nonetheless.

| [** READ THE FULL ARTICLE ON _THE ECONOMIST_ ->**](http://links.vivek2024.com/u/click?_t=07471d1165224e98aee1aca8cd71f6e2&_m=88380004ab77480ab137c69da7eabb94&_e=70G0v4hsB7xuXWMrzghYv3hVoYGBMzWcYkoP01gowHNRr97pcLK3vRGcAaxeQaEqHgLCyjmhdaUWzUGMI0EzFiR_qKwPTSR1QksYadYRAJY8WI-sUYXyfVN0ED7LXcewIqDyscvZSVWkyVmXLBot1kbdusoxJgYhFnLobwgq99BQl_fyow32SRTSBMWBP-3P4OE_zlcEdX6wptaHQ0QAxCR35Hr3ugE-uW2FinZBJGY6QRp-G4t1jwkvwi9_K5BByBNReqW45FnzScJsZLcinK9CbenyfFH_uy2owQ5zMGNjqAg-PpYDXtaNxCIwtM4A4XsYc-UVx8WbbaIsMJVCc65l3BSZ-lC5NF0Z4C0vWS8%3D)
---

At first blush, the two may seem unconnected. The First Amendment protects very different rights than the Equal Protection Clause of the 14th Amendment, after all. What could violations of students' free-speech rights have to do with a violation of students' right to be judged in a race-neutral manner at the point of admission?

A lot, it turns out. That is because the Supreme Court justified the use of admissions policies that take race into account in _Grutter v Bollinger_ , the ruling in 2003 that confirmed affirmative action as constitutional, solely as a means of achieving "livelier" and "more robust" campus discussions. Such admissions policies would lead to a more viewpoint-diverse class, the reasoning went, which would yield crucial educational benefits in the form of richer, more stimulating debate. But by stifling political discourse through heavy-handed policies, universities have in practice shown nothing but disdain for the very interest they claim is so "compelling" when seeking to use race-based admissions policies.

There's no question that when it comes to muzzling free speech, Harvard is one of the worst offenders. I can speak to this personally, as a member of the committee tasked with finding a replacement for Lawrence Summers—the popular dean who was forced to resign in 2006, in part for expressing the unacceptable view that there might be a biological basis for gender-based differences in intelligence.

Since then, the problem has only got worse. As of last year Harvard ranked 170th out of 203 American universities on free-speech metrics, according to the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, a civil-liberties group. In recent years it has disinvited speakers with controversial views, allowed students to disrupt pro-life events, fired a professor over a newspaper column that "demonised" Islam, and withdrawn a fellowship offer owing to the applicant's purported "anti-Israel bias". Tellingly, more than half of Harvard students who responded to the 2023 College Free Speech Rankings survey reported self-censoring. Three-quarters were worried (50% "a little", 25% "a lot") about damaging their reputation because someone might misunderstand something they said.

In April more than a hundred members of Harvard's faculty banded together to expose the university's silencing of those with non-Harvard-approved views. "We are in a crisis time right now," one professor explained. "Many, many people are being threatened with - and actually put through - disciplinary processes for their exercise of free speech and academic freedom."

How, then, can Harvard claim that robust campus debate is such a compelling interest that the university should be able to take the extraordinary measure of discriminating against Asian-American applicants on the basis of their race? It can't. At least not with a straight face.

[** READ THE FULL ARTICLE ON _THE ECONOMIST_ ->**](http://links.vivek2024.com/u/click?_t=07471d1165224e98aee1aca8cd71f6e2&_m=88380004ab77480ab137c69da7eabb94&_e=70G0v4hsB7xuXWMrzghYv3hVoYGBMzWcYkoP01gowHNRr97pcLK3vRGcAaxeQaEqHgLCyjmhdaUWzUGMI0EzFiR_qKwPTSR1QksYadYRAJY8WI-sUYXyfVN0ED7LXcewIqDyscvZSVWkyVmXLBot1kbdusoxJgYhFnLobwgq99BQl_fyow32SRTSBMWBP-3P4OE_zlcEdX6wptaHQ0QAxIcmJrrOgsVlgQyx5I2btSF_JZBhxOuVospyhdYrnp__95oNAIL39tzaD9lGyBmB7RuVm4-fp8ps4mmhrApRnews8aeHL_42x-LOvApN-F_1H1cUuf_p3v5JM4M6OUOB0Qq8-rQdch8DQIxwmAWjEfs%3D)
---

Of course, Harvard claims that it does not discriminate against Asian-American applicants, but the admissions numbers tell a different story. The university needs to take race into account in its admissions process - which in practice has meant excluding equally capable Asian-Americans from its student body - in order to, as it wrote to the justices, "cultivate the kinds of environments in which the richest exchange of ideas can flourish".

In fairness, many supporters of affirmative action have acknowledged that the viewpoint-diversity rationale is just a ruse. "Let's be honest," Randall Kennedy, a professor at Harvard Law School, has written. "Many who defend affirmative action for the sake of ‘diversity' are actually motivated by...social justice." Such people would "defend affirmative action even if social science demonstrated uncontrovertibly that diversity (or its absence) has no effect (or even a negative effect) on the learning environment."

Professor Kennedy is not alone. "The commitment to diversity is not real," Samuel Issacharoff, a professor at Columbia Law School, has said. "None of these universities has an affirmative-action program for Christian fundamentalists, Muslims, orthodox Jews or any other group that has a distinct viewpoint."

Of course, it is possible, even likely, that the Supreme Court would have overruled _Grutter_ even if universities had practised what they preached when it comes to valuing intellectual diversity and debate. The logic of the court's opinion before its latest ruling was pretty racist even on its own terms: people of certain races all think the same way, so universities should be allowed to engage in racial-balancing as a proxy for viewpoint-balancing, to improve classroom conversation.

Seriously? That view is also hard to square with the constitution itself. As the lawyer who represented the schoolchildren in Brown v Board of Education explained in 1952, "No State has any authority under the equal-protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to use race as a factor in affording educational opportunities among its citizens." The Equal Protection Clause hasn't changed since then.

In the end, the _Grutter_ decision may have been on life support anyway. But Harvard would have stood a better chance if it had at least pretended to care about fostering intellectual debate on campus. Instead, it all but stamped it out.

clean_body: I'm glad the U.S. Supreme Court finally laid to rest one of the worst failed experiments in American history: affirmative action. | | Fellow American, With its decision in Students for Fair Admissions v Harvard , handed down on June 29th, America's Supreme Court has finally laid affirmative action to rest. University administrators will surely be weeping at the grave. But what these administrators fail to appreciate is that they themselves may be accomplices in the doctrine's demise. Their weapon of choice was an unusual one: trampling free speech on campus by enacting speech codes, showing bias against students with disfavoured views and disinviting controversial speakers. Unusual, but deadly nonetheless. | At first blush, the two may seem unconnected. The First Amendment protects very different rights than the Equal Protection Clause of the 14th Amendment, after all. What could violations of students' free-speech rights have to do with a violation of students' right to be judged in a race-neutral manner at the point of admission? A lot, it turns out. That is because the Supreme Court justified the use of admissions policies that take race into account in Grutter v Bollinger , the ruling in 2003 that confirmed affirmative action as constitutional, solely as a means of achieving "livelier" and "more robust" campus discussions. Such admissions policies would lead to a more viewpoint-diverse class, the reasoning went, which would yield crucial educational benefits in the form of richer, more stimulating debate. But by stifling political discourse through heavy-handed policies, universities have in practice shown nothing but disdain for the very interest they claim is so "compelling" when seeking to use race-based admissions policies. There's no question that when it comes to muzzling free speech, Harvard is one of the worst offenders. I can speak to this personally, as a member of the committee tasked with finding a replacement for Lawrence Summers—the popular dean who was forced to resign in 2006, in part for expressing the unacceptable view that there might be a biological basis for gender-based differences in intelligence. Since then, the problem has only got worse. As of last year Harvard ranked 170th out of 203 American universities on free-speech metrics, according to the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, a civil-liberties group. In recent years it has disinvited speakers with controversial views, allowed students to disrupt pro-life events, fired a professor over a newspaper column that "demonised" Islam, and withdrawn a fellowship offer owing to the applicant's purported "anti-Israel bias". Tellingly, more than half of Harvard students who responded to the 2023 College Free Speech Rankings survey reported self-censoring. Three-quarters were worried (50% "a little", 25% "a lot") about damaging their reputation because someone might misunderstand something they said. In April more than a hundred members of Harvard's faculty banded together to expose the university's silencing of those with non-Harvard-approved views. "We are in a crisis time right now," one professor explained. "Many, many people are being threatened with - and actually put through - disciplinary processes for their exercise of free speech and academic freedom." How, then, can Harvard claim that robust campus debate is such a compelling interest that the university should be able to take the extraordinary measure of discriminating against Asian-American applicants on the basis of their race? It can't. At least not with a straight face. Of course, Harvard claims that it does not discriminate against Asian-American applicants, but the admissions numbers tell a different story. The university needs to take race into account in its admissions process - which in practice has meant excluding equally capable Asian-Americans from its student body - in order to, as it wrote to the justices, "cultivate the kinds of environments in which the richest exchange of ideas can flourish". In fairness, many supporters of affirmative action have acknowledged that the viewpoint-diversity rationale is just a ruse. "Let's be honest," Randall Kennedy, a professor at Harvard Law School, has written. "Many who defend affirmative action for the sake of ‘diversity' are actually motivated by...social justice." Such people would "defend affirmative action even if social science demonstrated uncontrovertibly that diversity (or its absence) has no effect (or even a negative effect) on the learning environment." Professor Kennedy is not alone. "The commitment to diversity is not real," Samuel Issacharoff, a professor at Columbia Law School, has said. "None of these universities has an affirmative-action program for Christian fundamentalists, Muslims, orthodox Jews or any other group that has a distinct viewpoint." Of course, it is possible, even likely, that the Supreme Court would have overruled Grutter even if universities had practised what they preached when it comes to valuing intellectual diversity and debate. The logic of the court's opinion before its latest ruling was pretty racist even on its own terms: people of certain races all think the same way, so universities should be allowed to engage in racial-balancing as a proxy for viewpoint-balancing, to improve classroom conversation. Seriously? That view is also hard to square with the constitution itself. As the lawyer who represented the schoolchildren in Brown v Board of Education explained in 1952, "No State has any authority under the equal-protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment to use race as a factor in affording educational opportunities among its citizens." The Equal Protection Clause hasn't changed since then. In the end, the Grutter decision may have been on life support anyway. But Harvard would have stood a better chance if it had at least pretended to care about fostering intellectual debate on campus. Instead, it all but stamped it out. Peter, Oregon lawmakers wrapped up the 2023 legislative session this past weekend, and I’m pleased to say we made solid progress on my mission-focused agenda. My top three priorities since Day One of my administration have been housing and homelessness, mental health and addiction services, and education and child care — **and we saw real, concrete action taken on all of these during the session. ** Over a billion dollars has been allocated to respond to the housing and homelessness crisis after I declared a state of emergency on my first day in office. We’ll be building new affordable housing, rehousing folks who need it, and bolstering resources to prevent evictions and homelessness in the first place. The legislature committed hundreds of millions of dollars for detox and rehab facilities, for the suicide prevention hotline, and for increasing access to life-saving overdose reversal kits. On education, we established targeted funding for early literacy, so all of Oregon’s students can learn to read and write because of science-based instruction in our schools and communities. We also created a child care infrastructure fund in order to increase access to affordable child care for more families. All this progress was done through the hard work and dedication of many folks — including you. The 2023 legislative session is over now, but our work isn’t done, which is why I’m asking you for your support once again. name: Tiernan Donohue
subject: Is there anything I can say before our deadline?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BOB CASEY FOR SENATE INC
body:
# [](https://go.bobcasey.com/go/181?t=1&akid=220%2E552475%2ET_X4AY)
Peter,
The first public fundraising deadline since we launched our re-election campaign is TOMORROW NIGHT, so I have to ask:**is there anything we can say that would inspire you to****[make your first donation to our campaign?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20230629-3?refcode=em20230629-3&refcode2=220_552475_T_X4AY&akid=220%2E552475%2ET_X4AY)**
What if I told you that Mitch McConnell confirmed PA’s Senate seat is one of his top targets?
What if I told you that national Republicans will spend millions upon millions running attack ads against Bob?
What if I told you that Democrats hold a slim 1-seat majority in the Senate, meaning that if we lose in Pennsylvania next year, we could lose the majority?
**[Yes, I'll Donate Now ››](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20230629-3?refcode=em20230629-3&refcode2=220_552475_T_X4AY&akid=220%2E552475%2ET_X4AY)**
What if I told you Bob isn’t done fighting to make the lives of hardworking Pennsylvania families easier?
What if I told you Republicans could use a Senate majority to cut programs like Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid, and undermine voting rights?
_What if I told you we are less than $15,100 away from reaching our end-of-quarter goal, and we can’t afford to fall even a little bit short?_
**[These are the stakes in our race, so I’ll ask one more time: Will you donate right now to help us reach our first end-of-quarter fundraising goal before tomorrow night?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/casey-em-20230629-3?refcode=em20230629-3&refcode2=220_552475_T_X4AY&akid=220%2E552475%2ET_X4AY)**

subject: We still have more to do.

body:
| | | Hi -- It’s Carole King.

Every day, we have a choice to make. Do we accept what is, or do we fight for a better future?

For caring Americans, a better future means protecting Social Security and Medicare so _everyone_ can retire with dignity. It means ensuring confirmation of judges who uphold our rights instead of stripping them away. And it means preserving our extraordinary national forests and implementing meaningful climate action.

**Every day, Senate Democrats are fighting for a better future for families, neighbors, and communities.**

Unfortunately, some Senate rules require more than a simple majority to get things done, and that’s why we need to EXPAND our Democratic majority in the Senate.

[**So will you please join me and pitch in $5 -- or whatever fits your budget -- to elect Democratic senators?**](https://go.dscc.org/go/14407?amount=5&t=4&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=5&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C50&code=DPE-FD-20230629-CaroleKing-CaroleKingReboot2v2-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20230629-CaroleKing-CaroleKingReboot2v2-Pros-sl1&akid=11170%2E9716520%2ETXXq2P)

Extreme right-wing forces give monumental amounts of money every day to elect Republicans who vote to drag us backwards.

**Our most powerful weapon against extreme right-wing forces is YOU.**

When caring Americans come together to vote, organize, and fight for families, neighbors, and communities -- our movement is stronger than anything Republican megadonors’ money can buy.

[**So, will you join me and thousands of other caring Americans by pitching in $5 before tomorrow's end-of-quarter deadline to expand Democrats’ crucial Senate majority?**](https://go.dscc.org/go/14407?amount=5&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=5&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C50&code=DPE-FD-20230629-CaroleKing-CaroleKingReboot2v2-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20230629-CaroleKing-CaroleKingReboot2v2-Pros-sl1&akid=11170%2E9716520%2ETXXq2P)

– Carole

# KLAYMAN: CHRISTIE IS A FAT BLOWHARD WHO BELIEVES MASS ILLEGAL SURVEILLANCE IS DANDY!
The Hill
Republican presidential candidate Chris Christie took aim at fellow 2024 GOP hopeful [Ron DeSantis,](https://freedomwatchusa.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=72bc9b8de1fa17e6901eb23e7&id=b1a1ba1b44&e=8edd2b8f7d) the governor of Florida, for dodging a question about the Jan. 6, 2021, attacks on the Capitol by saying that he was nowhere near the Capitol that day.“He wasn’t anywhere near Washington. Did he have a TV? Was he alive that day? Did he see what was going on?
I mean, that’s one of the most ridiculous answers I’ve heard in this race so far,” Christie, a former New Jersey governor, [told CNN’s Kaitlin Collins](https://freedomwatchusa.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=72bc9b8de1fa17e6901eb23e7&id=ab85ad8ec5&e=8edd2b8f7d) late Wednesday.

Hi Friend,
We are thrilled to share an update of our 2023 WVDP Summer Internship Project . This project represents a significant step in WVDP’s commitment to fostering talent, supporting professional development, and creating a pathway for future political involvement.
We believe in the power of mentorship, hands-on experience, and collaboration to shape the next generation of exceptional political leaders. WVDP’s internship project is designed to provide aspiring individuals with a unique opportunity to gain practical skills, industry insights, and a deep understanding of our organization's operations.
For the first time in recent history, we are pleased to be joined by nine dynamic college students and young professionals who have a passion for creating positive change through the political process in WV.
WVDP interns will be participating in weekly trainings and completing crafted actions that help them learn about and engage in both the political process and grassroots organizing.

body:
Let me share a little more about how we got to this point.
#
The last six months have been incredible, Peter.
From launching this campaign on January 6th to calling out Josh Hawley on cable news to breaking Missouri fundraising records, your support has helped us put a national spotlight on this U.S. Senate race. And now, our next major FEC deadline is less than 48 hours away.
In a moment, I’m going to ask you to **[chip in $10 or whatever you can toward our goal of raising 30,000 individual donations before midnight tomorrow.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) But first, let me share a little more about how we got here.**
**[ADD A DONATION NOW](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)
I grew up in Central Missouri. And like so many other Americans, my family lived paycheck-to-paycheck. So when my little sister was born with a heart condition, the medical bills bankrupted us. Maxed-out credit cards and no money left, times had never been tougher.
But we weren’t alone — our community took care of us. When my parents had to take my sister to the hospital in St. Louis, our neighbors and friends took my siblings and me into their homes and brought more meals by the house than we could ever hope to eat. **That’s the Missouri I grew up in.**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)
Their support helped send me to college, and after that I joined the Marines to honor everything they had done for me and my family growing up. Got deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan. Later the Pentagon. I was on the Joint Staff negotiating arms control agreements with NATO and Russia.
When I came home between tours in Iraq and Afghanistan, one of the hardest things was seeing what was happening back in my old neighborhood. It was a community picked for parts — the local corner store boarded up, my first family house bulldozed to the ground. **Here’s all that’s left of it:**
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)
While all of us were risking our lives building up towns like Habbaniyah, Fallujah, and Herat, career politicians like Josh Hawley let our country waste away. They spent trillions on bailouts, tax breaks, and subsidies for the industries that stripped our communities for parts — like Wall Street, Big Pharma, and Big Oil — and then told us they can’t figure out how to invest even a fraction of that into building up our own country and investing in our own people.
**I saw what was happening — and I was ready to fight back.**
So in my final year of active duty, I worked to upend the corporate defense monopolies that leave our country less safe. I also joined an organization that fights corporate monopolies — we took on defense contractors, Big Pharma, Big Tech, Big Ag, Wall Street. The people buying off our politicians and leaving the rest of us behind.
**And now, I’m running for U.S. Senate to replace Josh Hawley and fundamentally change who has power in our country** — so everyday people call the shots, not massive corporations or corrupt politicians. I want to abolish corporate PACs, expose lobbyists writing our laws, criminalize war profiteering, ban insider trading among members of Congress, and enact a Marshall Plan for the Midwest — a massive investment and job creation program that will rebuild our forgotten communities and get us off fossil fuels once and for all.
I want to codify Roe v. Wade, secure voting rights, and ban anti-union “Right-to-Work” scams forever. I want to put working people in charge of our country. But I need your help to get it done.
**Without a single cent of corporate PAC money, we’re building a people-powered movement to defeat Josh Hawley and flip this Senate seat — and I need you on our team.[Please add a donation of any amount toward our end-of-quarter goal right now so we can continue building this movement and finally give power back to working people.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=6&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)**
If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly:
[Contribute $10](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=7&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Contribute $25](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=8&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=9&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)
---
I’m not just running to make a point — **this is a race we can win.**
**Josh Hawley is vulnerable.** In 2018, he won his seat with only 51% of the vote — but after he exposed himself to be a fraud and a coward on January 6th, his approval has dropped to 42%. In Missouri’s last Senate race during a presidential election, the margin was only 2.7%.
Since then, Missourians have broken with Hawley and taken back their power at the ballot box by voting to raise the minimum wage, expand Medicaid through the Affordable Care Act, and legalize cannabis.
TIME Magazine called me the “clean-cut, populist Marine veteran who could give Democrats a fighting chance." And if we’re able to get this message in front of voters early in this race, we have a real shot at defeating Josh Hawley in 2024 and flipping Missouri’s U.S. Senate seat.
**But I need you on this team to get it done, Peter.** GOP insiders and even Hawley’s own campaign have already started attacking me — and over the coming months, they’re bound to get even more vicious. That’s why we need to start preparing right now to fight back and deliver our positive message to voters.
**[Will you chip in anything you can right now so we can hit our end-of-quarter goal and stay prepared for the fight ahead? I don’t take a cent from corporate PACs, so I mean it when I say anything makes a big difference to our campaign.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=10&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)**
If you've stored your info with ActBlue Express, we'll process your contribution instantly:
[Contribute $10](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=10&t=11&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Contribute $25](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=25&t=12&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Contribute $30](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=30&t=13&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Contribute $50](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=50&t=14&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Contribute $100](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=100&t=15&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Contribute $250](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34717?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amount=250&t=16&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3) [Give another amount](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/34716?refcode=em20230629-3334&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=17&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)
---
Together, we can take back power from the corrupt politicians like Josh Hawley and finally put real, everyday people in charge of our country.
Thanks for helping us get it done,
Lucas Kunce

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lk-email-footer?refcode=em20230629-3334-footer&t=18&refcode2=3334_614464_w34zz3&akid=3334%2E614464%2Ew34zz3)**

Hi there - Let me introduce myself: I’m Buddy Wheatley and I’m proud to be running for Kentucky Secretary of State, alongside Governor Andy Beshear.
When you come from a family that’s lived here for 150 years, being a Kentuckian becomes a part of your DNA.
I’ve played high school football here, went to the University of Kentucky, got married here, followed my father, grandfather and great-grandfather’s footsteps and pursued a career in public service as a firefighter - and eventually as a state representative.
When you’re a firefighter, your job is to always respond to the call. You can’t shy away from tough challenges. That’s why in the state legislature, I fought to expand access to the ballot box alongside Governor Beshear, including reforms that helped folks safely vote during the 2020 pandemic election.
But after the 2020 election, Secretary Michael Adams allowed these laws to revert back - and Kentucky once again became one of the most restrictive states in the country when it comes to access to the polls.
I’m ready to change that. And that’s why I’m running for Secretary of State. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dasspac-wheatley-june23?refcode=em_fr_b1_062923_buddy-surrogate_30AC&amount=10]
As Secretary of State, my top priority is to increase voter turnout. That means ensuring our elections are fully funded, expanding access to the ballot box, and partnering with our school system to educate our youth.
But I can’t do this alone. This race is going to be expensive and I’m going to need grassroots donors like you on my team.
That’s why I’m humbly asking you to make a split donation between my campaign and DASS PAC so we can win in November and protect our democracy. Can you donate now? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/dasspac-wheatley-june23?refcode=em_fr_b1_062923_buddy-surrogate_30AC&amount=10]

Hi friend – before I ask you to chip in to help me win in Ohio and keep the Senate blue, I need to take a moment to explain why I'm in this fight and what your grassroots contribution would mean today. I grew up in Mansfield, Ohio, in a community of ironworkers, carpenters, autoworkers, and electricians. I spent summers working on my family's farm. Today, I live in Cleveland with my wife, Connie, and our two rescue dogs, Franklin and Walter. **I’ll be honest with you, friend: **The Ohio I live in now looks a lot different from the one I grew up in. Over the years, we've seen manufacturing jobs shipped overseas because of bad trade deals, prices skyrocketing as wages failed to keep up, and hopes for a comfortable retirement dashed. That's why I've devoted my life to fighting for the Dignity of Work – the idea that hard work should pay off for everyone, no matter who you are, where you live, or what kind of work you do.

| Friend, I'm running to defeat Ted Cruz because this fight is personal for me. I'd love to take a moment to explain why.

I'm a fourth-generation Texan. I'm the proud son of a single mom who taught in public schools and sometimes worked a second job just to make ends meet.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65650874/414104744/-320404881?amount=25&refcode=EM_NBI_DWSPAC_20230629_FR_EOQ.2.10_0_12MO_colinallred_NA_NA_eoq.split&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOTc5MzMwYS1iYTE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u4RjfE6tPW90hEEwovat-LdN_kc8KdZEL5Gt9yKYSQI=)
Growing up, my world was pretty small. I never imagined I'd be working in the halls of Congress let alone taking on Ted Cruz, hoping to become the first Black senator from Texas. But I did dream of helping people – whether it was as Superman or a firefighter.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65650876/414104746/-320404881?amount=25&refcode=EM_NBI_DWSPAC_20230629_FR_EOQ.2.10_0_12MO_colinallred_NA_NA_eoq.split&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOTc5MzMwYS1iYTE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u4RjfE6tPW90hEEwovat-LdN_kc8KdZEL5Gt9yKYSQI=)
After playing football at Baylor University and in the NFL, I went to law school and became a civil rights attorney, specializing in voting rights.

I've watched this fundamental right be attacked and eroded my whole life – right here in Texas we have some of the most restrictive voter laws in the country, and it's no secret that these laws target Black and Brown voters.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65650879/414104747/-320404881?amount=25&refcode=EM_NBI_DWSPAC_20230629_FR_EOQ.2.10_0_12MO_colinallred_NA_NA_eoq.split&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOTc5MzMwYS1iYTE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u4RjfE6tPW90hEEwovat-LdN_kc8KdZEL5Gt9yKYSQI=)
**It was one of the great honors of my life that one of my heroes and a voting rights and American giant, Congressman John Lewis, joined me on the campaign trail in 2018. I beat the odds – and an 11-term GOP incumbent – to win that race and help Democrats flip the House. Now I'm ready to do it again and replace Ted Cruz in the U.S. Senate – but I need your help._[That's why I'm asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Democrats Win Seats today →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65650886/414104748/-320404881?amount=25&refcode=EM_NBI_DWSPAC_20230629_FR_EOQ.2.10_0_12MO_colinallred_NA_NA_eoq.split&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOTc5MzMwYS1iYTE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u4RjfE6tPW90hEEwovat-LdN_kc8KdZEL5Gt9yKYSQI=)_**

We've all watched for 10 years as Ted Cruz has failed the people of Texas repeatedly. He's bowed down to Donald Trump, pushed dangerous conspiracy theories about the 2020 elections, cheered on the rioters that stormed the Capitol on Jan. 6 and abandoned our state while Texans froze in the dark. To add insult to injury, after we passed critical voting rights legislation in the House, he spearheaded the effort to kill it in the Senate.

**Time and time again, Ted Cruz has made it clear he will always put Ted Cruz first. That's not me. I'm running for Senate to be a voice for all Texans, for families like yours and mine, and I hope you'll help me get there, friend. Because the truth is, unseating Ted Cruz won't be easy. But I’ve learned that even the most difficult task can be accomplished with the right team and the right plan of action. if we all work together and amass a grassroots movement like Texas has never seen, we can get this done but I need you with me.

_[So please, will you split a donation of $5, $10 or whatever you can between my campaign and Democrats Win Seats to help me defeat Ted Cruz, flip Texas blue and expand our Democratic Senate majority? Every dollar makes a difference in our battleground race, and I truly appreciate it →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/65650889/414104749/-320404881?amount=25&refcode=EM_NBI_DWSPAC_20230629_FR_EOQ.2.10_0_12MO_colinallred_NA_NA_eoq.split&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzkvMS84ODcwOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwOTc5MzMwYS1iYTE2LWVlMTEtYTliYi0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=u4RjfE6tPW90hEEwovat-LdN_kc8KdZEL5Gt9yKYSQI=)_**

Thanks for reading my story – and for being on my team. I can't tell you what it means to have you with me in this fight from the very beginning.

Colin Allred
